The exodromy correspondence of Barwick, Glasman, and Haine computes constructible sheaves of spaces on a scheme $X$ as an $\infty$-category of continuous functors from the profinite category $\operatorname{Gal}(X)$. Viewing $\operatorname{Gal}(X)$ instead as a condensed category, this was extended by Wolf to an exodromy correspondence for pro-étale sheaves. Using the condensed perspective from the outset, we give a quick and self-contained proof of the pro-étale exodromy theorem. This is used to extract an exodromy theorem for (Postnikov complete) étale sheaves that does not yet appear in the literature, which is closely related to Lurie's work on ultracategories. Finally, we use this to give a new proof of the constructible étale exodromy correspondence of Barwick, Glasman, and Haine. Without additional effort, our method removes the qcqs hypotheses on the schemes, and gives versions for sheaves with coefficients in more general $\infty$-categories. Finally, we refine the methods to obtain a $κ$-condensed statement for any uncountable cardinal $κ$ such that $κ> \lvert \mathcal O_X(U) \rvert$ for every affine open $U \subseteq X$.

Introduction Background If X X is a reasonable topological space, the monodromy correspondence gives an equivalence between locally constant sheaves on X X with values in a presentable ∞ \infty -category ℰ \mathscr{E} and the functor category Fun ⁡ ( Π ∞ ​ ( X ) , ℰ ) \Fun(\Pi_{\infty}(X),\mathscr{E}) . For a scheme X X , a similar description is given for locally constant sheaves of finite sets (or, more generally, π \pi -finite spaces ) using the étale fundamental group π 1 e ´ ​ t ​ ( X ) \pi_{1}^{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}(X) [ 15 , Exp. V] , [ 12 , Exp. X, §6] , [ 9 , §7] (resp. étale homotopy type Π ∞ e ´ ​ t ​ ( X ) \Pi_{\infty}^{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}(X) [ 5 , 13 , 22 ] ). This categorical description of locally constant sheaves on a topological space was extended to constructible sheaves by MacPherson (unpublished, first presented in Treumann’s thesis [ 45 , 46 ] ), and Lurie obtained an ∞ \infty -categorical version [ 29 , Thm. A.9.3] . An étale version was proven by Barwick, Glasman, and Haine [ 7 , Thm. 12.1.6] , who coined the term exodromy correspondence : Theorem 0 (Barwick–Glasman–Haine). —- Let X X be a qcqs scheme. Then there is an exodromy correspondence Sh cons ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t , 𝒮 ) → ∼ Fun cts ⁡ ( Gal ⁡ ( X ) , 𝒮 π ) \Sh_{{\operatorname{cons}}}(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}},\mathcal{S})\xrightarrow{\sim}\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}(\Gal(X),\mathcal{S}_{\pi}) between the ∞ \infty -category of constructible sheaves of spaces on X X and the ∞ \infty -category of continuous functors from the Galois category of X X to π \pi -finite spaces. Here, the Galois category Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) is a pro-object in π \pi -finite layered ∞ \infty -categories whose ‘materialisation’ (limit in Cat ∞ \Cat_{\infty} ) is the 1 1 -category Pts ∗ ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) = Fun ∗ ⁡ ( Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) , Set ) \Pts^{*}(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}})=\Fun^{*}(\Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}),\Set) of points of the étale topos Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) \Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}) , and continuous functors means functors in Pro ⁡ ( Cat ∞ ) \Pro(\Cat_{\infty}) , where 𝒮 π \mathcal{S}_{\pi} is treated as the constant pro-system. Any profinite ∞ \infty -category, such as Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) , can be viewed as a consensed (or pyknotic ) ∞ \infty -category by taking the limit in Cond ⁡ ( Cat ∞ ) \Cond(\Cat_{\infty}) of the diagram of ‘discrete’ ∞ \infty -categories, as in [ 7 , §13.5] . Writing 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) \mathbf{Gal}(X) for the condensed ∞ \infty -category defined by Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) , Wolf [ 49 , Cor. 1.2] extended the theorem above to a pro-étale exodromy theorem: Theorem 0 (Wolf). —- Let X X be a qcqs scheme. Then there is an exodromy correspondence Sh hyp ⁡ ( X pro ​ e ´ ​ t , 𝒮 ) → ∼ Fun cts ⁡ ( 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) , 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐝 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) ) . \Sh^{\operatorname{hyp}}(X_{\operatorname{pro\acute{e}t}},\mathcal{S})\xrightarrow{\sim}\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}(\mathbf{Gal}(X),\mathbf{Cond}(\mathcal{S})). Here 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐝 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \mathbf{Cond}(\mathcal{S}) is the condensed ∞ \infty -category taking a profinite space S S to Cond ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) / S \Cond(\mathcal{S})_{/S} (equivalently, Sh ⁡ ( ProFin / S , 𝒮 ) \Sh(\ProFin_{/S},\mathcal{S}) ), and continuous functors are functors of condensed ∞ \infty -categories. Main results In this paper, we take up a condensed perspective from the outset to give independent (and, in the author’s opinion, more geometric, more direct, and more uniform) proofs of the theorems of Barwick–Glasman–Haine and Wolf, as well as a number of generalisations and variants. Using a direct definition of the condensed Galois category 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) \mathbf{Gal}(X) (see Construction of the Galois category further down in this introduction), we obtain a quick geometric proof of the following generalisation of Wolf’s theorem: Theorem 1 ( Subsection 3.1 ). —- Let X X be a scheme, and let ℰ \mathscr{E} be an ∞ \infty -category that has small limits. Then there is an exodromy correspondence ℰ ​ 𝓍 : Sh hyp ⁡ ( X pro ​ e ´ ​ t , ℰ ) → ∼ Fun cts ⁡ ( 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) , 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐝 ⁡ ( ℰ ) ) , \mathcal{Ex}\colon\Sh^{\operatorname{hyp}}(X_{\operatorname{pro\acute{e}t}},\mathscr{E})\xrightarrow{\sim}\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}(\mathbf{Gal}(X),\mathbf{Cond}(\mathscr{E})), where 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐝 ⁡ ( ℰ ) \mathbf{Cond}(\mathscr{E}) is the condensed ∞ \infty -category taking a profinite space S S to Sh ⁡ ( ProFin / S , ℰ ) \Sh(\ProFin_{/S},\mathscr{E}) . To extract the constructible étale exodromy from the one for pro-étale hypersheaves, we first prove that the pro-étale exodromy correspondence restricts to a statement for Postnikov complete étale sheaves: Theorem 2 ( Subsection 3.2 ). —- Let X X be a scheme, and let ℰ \mathscr{E} be a compactly assembled presentable ∞ \infty -category. Then the pro-étale exodromy correspondence restricts to an étale exodromy correspondence ℰ ​ 𝓍 e ´ ​ t : Sh post ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t , ℰ ) → ∼ Fun cts ⁡ ( 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) , ℰ ¯ ) , \mathcal{Ex}^{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}\colon\Sh^{\post}(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}},\mathscr{E})\xrightarrow{\sim}\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}(\mathbf{Gal}(X),\underline{\mathscr{E}}), where ℰ ¯ \underline{\mathscr{E}} is the condensed ∞ \infty -category S ↦ Sh ⁡ ( S , ℰ ) S\mapsto\Sh(S,\mathscr{E}) . Note that ℰ ¯ \underline{\mathscr{E}} is a condensed ∞ \infty -category by [ 17 , Cor. 2.8] (this relies on the hypothesis that ℰ \mathscr{E} is compactly assembled). Even for ℰ = 𝒮 \mathscr{E}=\mathcal{S} , the result above does not appear in the literature, although Clark Barwick had already indicated awareness of a version of this result before the conception of the present paper. When ℰ = Set \mathscr{E}=\Set and X X is qcqs, this is almost the same statement as Lurie’s version of Makkai’s strong conceptual completeness theorem [ 32 , Thm. 0.0.6] . However, there is a small but important technical difference, which we comment on in Subsection 3.2 . Finally, we obtain a new proof of the constructible étale exodromy theorem of Barwick–Glasman–Haine: Theorem 3 ( Subsection 3.3 ). —- Let X X be a scheme. Then the étale exodromy correspondence restricts to a constructible étale exodromy correspondence ℰ 𝓍 cons e ´ ​ t : Sh cons ( X e ´ ​ t , 𝒮 ) → ∼ Fun cts ( 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ( X ) , 𝒮 ¯ ) cons , \mathcal{Ex}^{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}_{{\operatorname{cons}}}\colon\Sh_{{\operatorname{cons}}}(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}},\mathcal{S})\xrightarrow{\sim}\Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}(\mathbf{Gal}(X),\underline{\mathcal{S}}{}_{{\operatorname{cons}}}), where 𝒮 ¯ cons \underline{\mathcal{S}}{}_{{\operatorname{cons}}} denotes the condensed ∞ \infty -category S ↦ Sh cons ⁡ ( S , 𝒮 ) S\mapsto\Sh_{{\operatorname{cons}}}(S,\mathcal{S}) . In particular, there are no qcqs hypotheses in Theorem 1 , Theorem 2 , and Theorem 3 . This would be impossible to achieve via the profinite methods of [ 7 ] , since the Galois category is only ‘locally profinite’ in general. On the other hand, using the condensed point of view, this extension can easily be bootstrapped from the known results in the qcqs case by observing that 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) \mathbf{Gal}(X) is a Zariski cosheaf of condensed ∞ \infty -categories (our proofs do not require treating the qcqs case separately). In fact, using Theorem 1 , we obtain the following Van Kampen type result: Theorem 4 ( Subsection 4.1 ). —- The functor 𝐆𝐚𝐥 : Sch → Cond ⁡ ( Cat ∞ ) \mathbf{Gal}\colon\Sch\to\Cond(\Cat_{\infty}) is a pro-étale hypercosheaf. This is similar to two Van Kampen statements for 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) \mathbf{Gal}(X) and Π ∞ pro ​ e ´ ​ t ​ ( X ) \Pi_{\infty}^{{\operatorname{pro\acute{e}t}}}(X) proved in [ 16 ] ; see 4.1 . Note that our results are weaker than those of [ 7 ] in some ways. We only obtain 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) \mathbf{Gal}(X) as a condensed category, and do not recover the profinite structure when X X is a qcqs scheme. Moreover, we do not get an exodromy equivalence for constructible étale sheaves with respect to a fixed stratification (however, a quick geometric proof of a 1-categorical constructible étale exodromy correspondence with respect to a fixed stratification was obtained in [ 47 ] ). We also do not pursue the question of classifying the ∞ \infty -topoi satisfying such a profinite exodromy correspondence, which was carried out in [ 7 , Thm. 9.3.1] in the form of an ∞ \infty -categorical Hochster duality. Construction of the Galois category Given a qcqs scheme X X , Barwick–Glasman–Haine construct the Galois category Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) as a pro-object in (layered) ∞ \infty -categories [ 7 , Def. 12.1.3] . As a functor from π \pi -finite layered ∞ \infty -categories to spaces, it is given by Π ↦ Map RTop ∞ coh ⁡ ( Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t , 𝒮 ) , Fun ⁡ ( Π , 𝒮 ) ) \Pi\mapsto\Map_{\RTop_{\infty}^{\operatorname{coh}}}(\Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}},\mathcal{S}),\Fun(\Pi,\mathcal{S})) [ 7 , 10.1.1] . When Π = B ​ G \Pi=BG for a finite group G G , coherent geometric morphisms Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t , 𝒮 ) → Fun ⁡ ( G , 𝒮 ) \Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}},\mathcal{S})\to\Fun(G,\mathcal{S}) classify G op G^{\operatorname{op}} -torsors over X X . In general, there is a similar description in terms of filtering functors Π op → Sh cons ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t , 𝒮 ) \Pi^{\operatorname{op}}\to\Sh_{{\operatorname{cons}}}(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}},\mathcal{S}) , which are roughly ‘ Π op \Pi^{\operatorname{op}} -torsors’ (see [ 33 , Ch. VII, Def. 8.1 and Cor. 9.2] for the statement for 1-topoi). Such objects have not been classically studied in algebraic geometry (although this could be interesting to work out). For a working algebraic geometer, to get a more concrete grip on the exodromy correspondence, it is desirable to have a more geometric description of the profinite category Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) . This is the starting point of this paper. As a first step, [ 7 , 12.1.5] gives a concrete description of the underlying category of the profinite category Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) (obtained by taking the limit in Cat ∞ \Cat_{\infty} ): this is given by the category of points Pts ∗ ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) \Pts^{*}(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}) of the étale topos, which by [ 3 , Exp. VIII, Thm. 7.9] is equivalent to the opposite of the category of strictly Henselian local rings with a weakly étale map to X X . It is classical that an étale sheaf ℱ \mathscr{F} comes equipped with cospecialisation maps ℱ x ¯ → ℱ y ¯ \mathscr{F}_{\bar{x}}\to\mathscr{F}_{\bar{y}} whenever x ∈ { y } ¯ x\in\overline{\{y\}} [ 3 , Exp. VIII, 7.7] . Thus, ignoring continuity issues, the étale exodromy functor of Theorem 2 and Theorem 3 should take ℱ \mathscr{F} to the functor Pts ∗ ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) → Set \Pts^{*}(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}})\to\Set taking x ¯ \bar{x} to the stalk ℱ x ¯ \mathscr{F}_{\bar{x}} , and taking a map Spec ⁡ 𝒪 X , y ¯ sh → Spec ⁡ 𝒪 X , x ¯ sh \Spec\mathcal{O}_{X,\bar{y}}^{\operatorname{sh}}\to\Spec\mathcal{O}_{X,\bar{x}}^{\operatorname{sh}} to the cospecialisation ℱ x ¯ → ℱ y ¯ \mathscr{F}_{\bar{x}}\to\mathscr{F}_{\bar{y}} . To prove an exodromy correspondence via this approach, what is missing is a description of the profinite topology on Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) . We note that Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) becomes a category internal to Stone spaces, so we need to describe a profinite set of objects and a profinite set of morphisms with a continuous composition operation. While [ 7 , 0.0.2] explains the profinite topology on Hom ⁡ ( x ¯ , y ¯ ) \Hom(\bar{x},\bar{y}) for geometric points x ¯ , y ¯ → X \bar{x},\bar{y}\to X , it is not clear how to describe a Stone space of all objects or of all morphisms in Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) . The reason this is difficult to do is that the categorically/homotopically meaningful ( 2 , 1 ) (2,1) -category of Stone categories is a localisation of category objects in Stone spaces along the collection of internal functors that are (internally) fully faithful and essentially surjective (see [ 26 , Thm. 1.2.13] for a version of this statement in an ∞ \infty -topos). Since surjections of Stone spaces do not always split, this means that such representatives are not unique, and to do this for Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) relies on making choices — similar to how a choice of pro-étale hypercover by w-strictly local schemes leads to a model for the pro-étale homotopy type, as suggested in [ 9 , Rmk. 4.2.9] and worked out in [ 20 , Appendix A] , [ 50 , Prop. 7.3.1.11] , and [ 16 , Rmk. 3.20] . Instead of addressing this question directly, we opt to work with condensed categories in favour of Stone categories, since internal category theory is better understood in an ( ∞ \infty -)topos. We replace the profinite definition of Gal ⁡ ( X ) \Gal(X) by a condensed one, defined as 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) : ProFin op \displaystyle\mathbf{Gal}(X)\colon\ProFin^{\operatorname{op}} → Cat \displaystyle\to\Cat S \displaystyle S ↦ Fun loc ​ coh ∗ ⁡ ( Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) , Sh ⁡ ( S ) ) . \displaystyle\mapsto\Fun^{*}_{{\operatorname{loc\ \!coh}}}(\Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}),\Sh(S)). Such a definition was already suggested by [ 7 , Ex. 13.5.4] (where the locally coherent condition is missing). A detailed comparison between the profinite and condensed Galois categories appeared in [ 50 , Prop. 7.1.2.8] (but see Subsection 2.1 ), which was partially motivated by the present paper (see Acknowledgements ) as well as by [ 16 ] . While this paper was in preparation, the above definition was also used as the definition in [ 16 , Def. 3.24] and [ 34 , Rec. 2.2.30] . In particular, while the results of the present paper are separate from those in [ 16 ] , the underlying philosophy is very similar. This condensed Galois category generalises the observation above that the ∗ * -points of 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) \mathbf{Gal}(X) are given by points of the étale topos Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) \Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}) . To prove the exodromy theorem, we also need a generalisation of the classification of points of the étale topos via strictly Henselian schemes. Extending [ 3 , Exp. VIII, Thm. 7.9] , we prove the following result: Theorem 5. —- Let X X be a scheme, and let Stone / X loc ​ coh → ProFin \Stone_{/X}^{{\operatorname{loc\ \!coh}}}\to\ProFin be the Grothendieck construction of the functor 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) : ProFin op → Cat \mathbf{Gal}(X)\colon\ProFin^{\operatorname{op}}\to\Cat . Then Stone / X loc ​ coh \Stone_{/X}^{{\operatorname{loc\ \!coh}}} is canonically equivalent to the category AffPro ​ E ´ ​ t / X wsl \AffProEt_{/X}^{\operatorname{wsl}} of w-strictly local schemes that are limits of affine schemes in E ´ ​ t / X \Et_{/X} . This is proved in Subsection 2.4 and Subsection 2.4 . An analogous result for arbitrary geometric morphisms from profinite sets to a coherent topos 𝒳 \mathscr{X} is also the key ingredient for Lurie’s proof of Makkai’s strong conceptual completeness theorem [ 32 , Thm. 6.3.14] . The statement of Subsection 2.4 in itself can be deduced from Lurie’s theorem, but we give a geometric proof in order to get the more refined versions of Subsection 2.4 and Subsection 2.4 . The translation from Lurie’s version to the one above was also noted (without proof) in Mair’s thesis [ 34 , Cor. 2.2.42] . On cardinality bounds This paper heavily uses the language of condensed mathematics. Working with sheaves on the category of profinite sets inevitably leads to set-theoretic issues. We resolve these by restricting to profinite sets that are small with respect to some sufficiently large cardinal κ \kappa . We prove a more precise version of Theorem 1 taking these cardinals into account; see Subsection 3.1 and Subsection 1.1 for a precise formulation. We do a little extra work to avoid additional hypotheses on the cardinal κ \kappa : it need neither be regular nor a strong limit cardinal. In particular, we do not have access to enough w-projective objects (see Subsection 1.2 ) in the pro-étale site. For example, this allows us to show that a version of Theorem 1 holds in the light condensed setting as long as 𝒪 X ​ ( U ) \mathscr{O}_{X}(U) is countable for every affine open U ⊆ X U\subseteq X . While it appears that the κ \kappa -condensed category 𝐆𝐚𝐥 κ ​ ( X ) \mathbf{Gal}_{\kappa}(X) of a scheme X X depends on a choice of auxiliary cardinal κ \kappa , we prove an accessibility result in §4.2 for the functor 𝐆𝐚𝐥 : ProFin op → Cat \mathbf{Gal}\colon\ProFin^{\operatorname{op}}\to\Cat , which implies that knowing 𝐆𝐚𝐥 κ ​ ( X ) \mathbf{Gal}_{\kappa}(X) for a single (sufficiently large) value of κ \kappa determines 𝐆𝐚𝐥 λ ​ ( X ) \mathbf{Gal}_{\lambda}(X) for every (sufficiently large) cardinal λ \lambda . Outline of the proofs We start by proving Theorem 5 by a similar strategy to [ 3 , Exp. VIII, Thm. 7.9] . Given a locally coherent geometric morphism s ∗ : Sh ⁡ ( S ) → Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) s_{*}\colon\Sh(S)\to\Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}) from a profinite set S S , we construct a Henselisation X ( s ) ∈ AffPro ​ E ´ ​ t / X wsl X_{(s)}\in\AffProEt_{/X}^{\operatorname{wsl}} of X X along s s , which is a w-strictly local affine scheme whose profinite set of connected components is canonically identified with S S . Then the subscheme of closed points Z = X ( s ) cl Z=X_{(s)}^{\operatorname{cl}} is zero-dimensional with separably algebraically closed residue fields, so Sh ⁡ ( Z e ´ ​ t ) ≃ Sh ⁡ ( S ) \Sh(Z_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}})\simeq\Sh(S) . We prove that s ∗ s_{*} is isomorphic to the pushforward Sh ⁡ ( Z e ´ ​ t ) → Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) \Sh(Z_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}})\to\Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}) , and that every w-strictly local scheme in AffPro ​ E ´ ​ t / X \AffProEt_{/X} arises in this way. With Theorem 5 in place, the proof of Theorem 1 proceeds as follows. The functor category Fun cts ⁡ ( 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) , 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐝 ⁡ ( ℰ ) ) \Fun^{\operatorname{cts}}(\mathbf{Gal}(X),\mathbf{Cond}(\mathscr{E})) may be viewed as a full subcategory of the category of ℰ \mathscr{E} -valued presheaves on the Grothendieck construction Stone / X loc ​ coh ≃ AffPro ​ E ´ ​ t / X wsl \Stone_{/X}^{{\operatorname{loc\ \!coh}}}\simeq\AffProEt_{/X}^{\operatorname{wsl}} . The same holds for Sh hyp ⁡ ( X pro ​ e ´ ​ t , ℰ ) \Sh^{\operatorname{hyp}}(X_{\operatorname{pro\acute{e}t}},\mathscr{E}) since AffPro ​ E ´ ​ t / X wsl \AffProEt_{/X}^{\operatorname{wsl}} forms a basis for the pro-étale topology, so it only remains to see that the descent conditions imposed on both subcategories agree. The key input for this verification is Subsection 1.3 , which shows that the pro-étale topology on AffPro ​ E ´ ​ t / X wsl \AffProEt_{/X}^{\operatorname{wsl}} agrees with the w-local topology ( Subsection 1.3 ), whose covers are jointly surjective families of w-local maps in AffPro ​ E ´ ​ t / X wsl \AffProEt_{/X}^{\operatorname{wsl}} . (When working with κ \kappa -condensed sets for a strong limit cardinal κ \kappa , the proof simplifies even further by restricting to w-projective schemes and extremally disconnected sets: instead of the w-local topology, we need only consider functors that take finite coproducts to products. See Subsection 3.1 for details.) To obtain Theorem 2 and Theorem 3 , we identify both sides of the étale and constructible exodromy correspondences as full subcategories of the ∞ \infty -categories appearing in Theorem 1 . To extract Sh post ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t , 𝒮 ) \Sh^{\post}(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}},\mathcal{S}) inside Sh hyp ⁡ ( X pro ​ e ´ ​ t , 𝒮 ) \Sh^{\operatorname{hyp}}(X_{\operatorname{pro\acute{e}t}},\mathcal{S}) , we use the criterion that truncated étale sheaves are exactly the truncated pro-étale sheaves that take filtered limits of affine pro-étale schemes to colimits; see Subsection 3.2 (this is a variant of [ 9 , Lem. 5.1.2] ). There is a similar description for Sh ⁡ ( S , 𝒮 ) \Sh(S,\mathcal{S}) inside Sh ⁡ ( ProFin / S , 𝒮 ) \Sh(\ProFin_{/S},\mathcal{S}) , which proves Theorem 2 . To recover Theorem 3 , we only need to observe that constructibility descends along surjective morphisms of schemes; see Subsection 3.3 . Structure of the paper We start in §1 with some preliminary results. In §1.1 , we set up the cardinality bounds used throughout the paper. This is followed up in §1.2 by a quick review of acyclic and w-strictly local schemes, as defined by Artin [ 6 , §3] and Bhatt–Scholze [ 9 , Def. 2.2.1] respectively. In §1.3 , we define a κ \kappa -small pro-étale site X κ ​ - ​ pro ​ e ´ ​ t X_{\kappa\text{-}{\operatorname{pro\acute{e}t}}} , as well as a new ( κ \kappa -small) w-local site X ( κ ​ - ) ​ wl X_{(\kappa\text{-}){\operatorname{wl}}} . Next, §2 is dedicated to the proof of Theorem 5 . In §2.1 , we give the definition of 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) \mathbf{Gal}(X) as a condensed category of points and relate it to the profinite definition of [ 7 ] . As in the classical computation of the category of points of Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) \Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}) [ 3 , Exp. VIII, Thm. 7.9] , we want to identify w-strictly local schemes W ∈ AffPro ​ E ´ ​ t / X W\in\AffProEt_{/X} with the functors Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) → Set \Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}})\to\Set they corepresent. In fact, since every clopen in W W corepresents such a functor, these glue together to a functor Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) → Sh ⁡ ( S ) \Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}})\to\Sh(S) where S = π 0 ​ ( W ) S=\pi_{0}(W) . We encode this extra data by exhibiting W W itself as (the global sections of) an S S -cosheaf in AffPro ​ E ´ ​ t / X \AffProEt_{/X} ; this theory is set up in §2.2 . In §2.3 , we define the Henselisation along a geometric morphism s ∗ : Sh ⁡ ( S ) → Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) s_{*}\colon\Sh(S)\to\Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}) , and show that they set up an equivalence between geometric morphisms s ∗ : Sh ⁡ ( S ) → Sh ⁡ ( X e ´ ​ t ) s_{*}\colon\Sh(S)\to\Sh(X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}}) and acyclic schemes W ∈ AffPro ​ E ´ ​ t / X W\in\AffProEt_{/X} with π 0 ​ ( W ) ≅ S \pi_{0}(W)\cong S (see Subsection 2.3 ). This is used in §2.4 to prove Theorem 5 (see Subsection 2.4 and Subsection 2.4 ). In §3 , we prove the pro-étale and étale exodromy theorems. The subsections §3.1 , §3.2 , and §3.3 are dedicated to the proofs of Theorem 1 , Theorem 2 , and Theorem 3 respectively, along the lines outlined above. We end in §4 with some formal properties of the condensed category of points: in §4.1 , we prove the Van Kampen theorem ( Theorem 4 ), and in §4.2 , we prove an accessibility result for the functor 𝐆𝐚𝐥 ⁡ ( X ) : ProFin op → Cat \mathbf{Gal}(X)\colon\ProFin^{\operatorname{op}}\to\Cat . In Appendix A , we include some general results on ∞ \infty -topoi that are used in §3 and §4 . The main results are the construction of a hypersheaf of large ∞ \infty -categories U ↦ Sh hyp ⁡ ( 𝒞 / U , ℰ ) U\mapsto\Sh^{\operatorname{hyp}}(\mathscr{C}_{/U},\mathscr{E}) on any ∞ \infty -site 𝒞 \mathscr{C} with values in any ∞ \infty -category ℰ \mathscr{E} with small limits ( Subsection A.1 ), and a computational tool for colimits of condensed ∞ \infty -categories ( Subsection A.2 ) that is used to prove Theorem 4 . Finally, Appendix B gives an alternative, more algebro-geometric, way to think about the classification of w-strictly local schemes of Subsection 2.4 . Notational conventions Our notations generally follow those of [ 2 , 3 , 4 , 44 ] on the one hand and [ 27 , 29 , 31 ] on the other. As in [ 27 , §1.2.15 and §5.4.1] , we assume the existence of sufficiently large strongly inaccessible cardinals. We will fix an uncountable strongly inaccessible cardinal once and for all (without name), and the notion of smallness is understood with respect to this cardinal. We will write Set \Set (resp. 𝒮 \mathcal{S} , Cat ∞ \Cat_{\infty} ) for the category (resp. ∞ \infty -category) of small sets (resp. (essentially) small spaces, (essentially) small ∞ \infty -categories [ 27 , §5.4.1] ). We will write 𝒮 ^ \widehat{\mathcal{S}} (resp. Cat ^ ∞ \widehat{\Cat}_{\infty} ) for the ∞ \infty -category of large spaces (resp. ∞ \infty -categories), which are assumed small in some (fixed and unnamed) larger universe. In an even larger universe, we write Cat ⁡ Cat ^ ^ ∞ \mathchoice{\widehat{\raisebox{1.72218pt}{\vphantom{$\Cat$}}\smash{\widehat{\Cat}}}}{\widehat{\raisebox{1.29167pt}{\vphantom{$\Cat$}}\smash{\widehat{\Cat}}}}{\widehat{\raisebox{-1.5pt}{\vphantom{$\Cat$}}\smash{\widehat{\Cat}}}}{\widehat{\raisebox{1.0pt}{\vphantom{$\Cat$}}\smash{\widehat{\Cat}}}}_{\infty} for the ∞ \infty -category of very large ∞ \infty -categories. Unless otherwise noted, all spaces will be assumed small, and all ∞ \infty -categories will be assumed large (i.e., in Cat ^ ∞ \widehat{\Cat}_{\infty} ). If 𝒞 \mathscr{C} is an ∞ \infty -site and ℰ \mathscr{E} an ∞ \infty -category, we write Sh ⁡ ( 𝒞 , ℰ ) \Sh(\mathscr{C},\mathscr{E}) for the ℰ \mathscr{E} -valued sheaves on 𝒞 \mathscr{C} (we recall this notion in Appendix A ). Because a substantial part of the arguments are 1-categorical, we will reserve the notation Sh ⁡ ( 𝒞 ) \Sh(\mathscr{C}) for Sh ⁡ ( 𝒞 , Set ) \Sh(\mathscr{C},\Set) when 𝒞 \mathscr{C} is a 1-site. We denote the category of topological spaces by Top \operatorname{Top} , and use RTop \RTop and LTop \LTop for the ( 2 , 1 ) (2,1) -category of topoi with right adjoints f ∗ f_{*} and left adjoints f ∗ f^{*} as morphisms, respectively. Likewise, RTop ∞ \RTop_{\infty} and LTop ∞ \LTop_{\infty} denote that ( ∞ , 1 ) (\infty,1) -category of ∞ \infty -topoi with right adjoints f ∗ f_{*} and left adjoints f ∗ f^{*} as morphisms, respectively. Lower versus higher categories The object of study in this paper is ℰ \mathscr{E} -valued sheaves on the étale and pro-étale sites of a scheme X X . We have separated the geometric and (1-categorical) site-theoretic arguments on X e ´ ​ t X_{\operatorname{\acute{e}t}} and X pro ​ e ´ ​ t X_{\operatorname{pro\acute{e}t}} (§1–2) from the higher categorical arguments about ℰ \mathscr{E} -valued sheaves (§3–4 and Appendix A ). In particular, the proof of Theorem 5 is entirely 1-categorical. Readers who are primarily interested in Set \Set - and Ab \Ab -valued sheaves should be able to make the required modifications in §3–4 to avoid higher category theory altogether. On the other hand, we chose to present the proof with the most general coefficients where it applies. For instance, applying this general version when ℰ \mathscr{E} is the stable ∞ \infty -category D ⁡ ( 𝐙 ) D(\mathbf{Z}) gives derived statements; see Subsection 3.1 and Subsection 3.2 . Since the algebraic closure of a finite field is countably infinite, our notion of smallness should not distinguish between finite and countable infinite sets. This motivates the following definitions.

Definition 1.2.1. —-: A scheme W W is acyclic if it is quasi-compact and every étale surjection U ↠ W U\twoheadrightarrow W has a section. This is the same definition as [ 6 , §3] , except that we always assume that W W is quasi-compact. We say that a scheme W W is w-strictly local if it is acyclic and the set of closed points W cl ⊆ W W^{\operatorname{cl}}\subseteq W is closed. This coincides with the definition of [ 9 , Def. 2.1.1 and Def. 2.2.1] since W W is automatically affine by Subsection 1.2 below.

Remark 1.2.2. —-: We will say that a scheme W W is w-projective if it is w-strictly local and π 0 ​ ( W ) \pi_{0}(W) is projective in compact Hausdorff spaces. Such schemes are called w-contractible in [ 9 , Def. 2.4.1] , but the condition is more similar to projectivity than contractibility.
